tier_reason: Raised D to C. Enricher e109 (2026-10-05) reached aras-p's independent 'Comparing BCn texture decoders' (2022-06-23) through the public aras-p/aras-p.hugo repo (content/blog/2022/06-bcn-decode-libraries.md and static/img/blog/2022/bcn-decode-*.png): a public harness (aras-p/bcn_decoder_tester, pinned submodules, 20 runs per DDS file, Windows preset RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2), Ryzen 9 5950X with VS2022 and clang 14, M1 Max with clang 13, bcdec e3ca0 against DirectXTex 679538e and others. That would support A on Windows, but the measured bcdec e3ca0 had rounding bugs later fixed (BC1 off by up to 1 per channel, issue #15; alpha +1 bias, issue #12; fixed 2024 with same-cost integer operations) and the harness only warns on hash mismatch, so under the project rule for numbers measured on code later fixed for correctness it stays at C. A re-run of the public harness on current bcdec would make it A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Independent (aras-p, 2022-06-23, derived from page data): against DirectXTex 679538e on a Ryzen 9 5950X with VS2022, bcdec e3ca0 BC1 1319 vs 272 Mpix/s (4.85x), BC3 704 vs 254 (2.77x), BC6H unsigned 85 vs 25 (3.40x), BC7 142 vs 93 (1.53x); with clang 14 on the same CPU BC1 1449 vs 223 (6.50x), BC3 621 vs 207 (3.00x), BC7 169 vs 127 (1.33x); on an M1 Max with clang 13 BC1 2088 vs 183 (11.4x), BC3 1093 vs 185 (5.91x), BC7 220 vs 140 (1.57x). Not the fastest everywhere: bc7enc_rdo's bc7decomp is 2.3-4.4x faster on BC7, etcpak 1.16-1.7x faster on BC1/BC3, and on the M1 bcdec's BC6H is behind ConvectionKernels, SwiftShader and Mesa. First-party PR #1 before/after: BC1 821 to 1327, BC3 516 to 694, BC6H 65 to 85, BC7 91 to 143 Mpix/s (VS2022, 5950X).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Windows: Visual Studio 2022 (cl) and clang 14 (clang-cl), bcn_decoder_tester preset RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2; macOS: clang 13, flags not given in the presets. bcdec commit e3ca0 vs DirectXTex 679538e, submodules pinned in the harness.
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X (Windows) and Apple M1 Max (macOS), single-threaded, 20 runs per file.
corrections.caveats: Independent harness and post by aras-p (source readable at raw.githubusercontent.com/aras-p/aras-p.hugo, content/blog/2022/06-bcn-decode-libraries.md; chart PNGs under static/img/blog/2022/). The measured bcdec e3ca0 had small rounding bugs later fixed with same-cost operations (BC1 off by up to 1 per channel, issue #15; alpha +1 bias, issue #12), and the harness only warns on output-hash mismatch, so speed was not inflated but the numbers predate the fixes (tier capped at C by project rule). bcdec is not the fastest decoder for BC7 (bc7enc_rdo 2.3-4.4x faster) or BC1/BC3 (etcpak 1.16-1.7x faster). The README disclaims speed as a goal.

tier_reason: Tier unchanged (C). Enricher e109 (2026-10-05) found the Qt, Cairo and Skia painter-cells ports that the verifier called unpublished: branch with_ports_of_painter-cells (2018-12-20) holds qt/cairo/skia_painter_cells, example-benchmark.sh, bench.sh, the Skia gn args and the Skia commit 01979132133e. Still C because CPU and GPU are unnamed, the numbers are snippet-only and the ports postdate the 2016 runs.

corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the numbers come from search-result text of Kevin Rogovin's XDC 2016 slides and the XDC 2016 abstract page (x.org, Phoronix, mail-archive and the Chromium graphics-dev post are egress-blocked here). First-party, single clipping-heavy demo, ten years old (Skia, Cairo and Qt of 2016). The Qt, Cairo and Skia painter-cells ports are public on the repo branch with_ports_of_painter-cells (2018-12-20: qt_painter_cells, cairo_painter_cells, skia_painter_cells, example-benchmark.sh, bench.sh, Skia gn args, Skia commit 01979132133e), but they postdate the 2016 runs and bench.sh has a typo ('vlank_mode=0'). Fairness flaw: the Skia port calls drawText every frame while FastUIDraw, Cairo and Qt pre-lay glyphs, so the Skia GL ratio favours FastUIDraw. The headline 9x compares GPU rendering against Cairo's CPU renderer; against Skia GL the win is about 4.9x to 8.2x (derived from snippet data). Issue #19: Mesa SWR 1.9 fps vs Cairo 32.7; issue #49: about 7x the CPU load of nanovg, never fixed. Intel archived the repository on 2023-01-07; last code commit 2019-12-20. Requires GL 3.3 or GLES 3.0 and, for non-Porter-Duff blends, framebuffer-fetch or fragment-shader-interlock.
